items.title: [RFC]: KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters
items.bodyExcerpt:
**Status:** Draft · **PRs:** #58207 (group size), #58380 (prefer `BLHNC`, stacked on #58207)

## TL;DR

Speculative drafters on hybrid models add a small KV cache bucket of their own, which breaks vLLM's KV cache grouping heuristic in two ways:

- **Too many groups (Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash):** a one-layer drafter bucket forces **one group per layer**: Qwen3.5-27B goes from 4 to 70 groups (#49730), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 4 to 46. Each group rebuilds attention metadata every step, so DFlash loses much of its speedup; forcing fewer groups today costs KV cache capacity.
- **Full attention padding (MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash):** the 5-layer drafter bucket sets the group size, which doesn't divide the target's 9 full attention layers, so a full attention padding layer is allocated for the whole context (#58175). Kimi-K3 + DSpark has the same problem: its 5-layer drafter bucket pads the 24 MLA (full attention) layers, with 20 groups.

Checked and unaffected (identical grouping with and without these PRs): GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark.

A two-part proposal fixes both:

| part | problem | fix | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · #58207** | small drafter buckets force per-layer KV groups, or full attn padding | pick the group size by worst-case padding **bytes**; `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) | 46 → **17** groups, **+54%** tok/s @c=1, **+36%** @c=32 | 11 → **7** groups, no full attn padding, KV capacity 5.76M → 5.96M |
| **2 · #58380** | `LBHNC` forces padding when drafter bytes/token ≠ target's | prefer `BLHNC` when the backends can run it and it avoids full attn padding or needs fewer groups | **5** groups, no padding, 7.53M tokens (> main's 7.42M); Triton only today | stays `LBHNC` at 7 groups (`BLHNC` would need 12 and has no full attn padding to remove) |

The parts are complementary: part 2 picks the path; part 1 is the fallback path (§5).

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix GLM45 reasoning token counting
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix GLM reasoning token accounting after the `glm45` and `glm47` reasoning parsers migrated to `Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`.

GLM starts in the reasoning state and may omit the opening `<think>` marker. The generic parser-engine counter starts at depth zero, so it reported zero reasoning tokens when generated output contained only `</think>` or no reasoning markers, even though the same parser extracted that output as reasoning.

This change adds GLM-specific `count_reasoning_tokens()` behavior while preserving the generic nested-marker logic:

- with `<think>`, reuse the parser-engine counter so prefixes before the marker are excluded;
- with only `</think>`, count tokens before the first closing marker;
- with no markers, count the full output, consistent with GLM reasoning extraction.

This affects reasoning token accounting only; it does not change generated model output, so no model accuracy evaluation is required.

Duplicate-work check: refreshed searches of open PRs for "GLM45 reasoning token count", "glm45 reasoning_tokens", and "Glm47MoeParser count_reasoning_tokens". No open PR other than this one addresses GLM `count_reasoning_tokens()` accounting.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.
- The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged.
- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

## Update: indexer and non-indexer layers are two KV cache groups

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53781  added the is_index_group_leader field to MLAAttentionSpec: `is_index_group_leader=self.indexer is not None,`. Layers can only share a KV cache group if they agree on is_index_group_leader, so once the flag is set per layer, indexer and non-indexer layers land in different groups and therefore get different metadata instances with separate paged_kv_indices

    ...
    and len(index_group_leader_set) == 1
    ...
), (
    "All attention layers in the same KV cache group must use the same "

)
```

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.
This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel.

This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty`
and the fill is removed.

## Safety

The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside
`[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial
load, so padding values are never read. The top-k result is unchanged.

The main goal is to improve performance for GLM 5.2 on MI355 by accelerating the sparse MLA attention using the new gluon backend, both for decode and prefill.

## Purpose

Two related changes, both following the review on this PR:

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A streaming tool call can end with `finish_reason` set while `arguments` is cut off mid-string. Any client that calls `json.loads` on the accumulated arguments fails on it. Reproduced live on Qwen3.8-27B in 7 of 25 requests sent straight at the worker, no proxy in the path.

`_safe_arg_prefix` (`parser_engine.py:299` on main at `8a2364605c0b`) deliberately streams unterminated string values for prefix-stable keys. Its own docstring (`:306-308`) carries the contract: "String values for keys in `string_keys` are prefix-stable, so stream their unterminated content instead of buffering long arguments until the closing tag arrives." Something has to close them, and that something is the flush.

`_flush_arg_converter` (`parser_engine.py:1052` on main) re-derives the arguments with `partial=False`. ## Purpose

Fixes #55080

items.title: [Kernel] persistent_topk: deterministic select, faster than the exact-topk workaround
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

1. **Ours.** We censused the top-k boundary on real traffic: **0 ties at the k-th value across 6,192
   selecting rows** at 16k context ([09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55122#issuecomment-5602743511)).
   93 % of rows had fewer visible blocks than k, so selection was a no-op.
2. **The reporter of #51782.** @xueyangcs states the HPC-Ops TopK contract is **set-exact only** —
   with ties, any valid top-k set is permitted; set-stability was never guaranteed
   ([#51782, 09-09](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).
3. **An independent field report.** @NNNtrance replaced the selection with an exact `torch.topk` on
   GLM-5.3-Flash across three DGX Sparks and got **9/6 bad turns vs 11/7 stock — within noise**,

Prefill `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` stores into `tail[blk]` using `blk = tslot // kpool`. Decode already skipped `block >= n_tail`; seed did not.

## Measured (gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4)

See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56037 **Crash D** (2026-09-07).

ShaderName : _kpool_tail_seed_kernel
Memory Fault Error
Memory access fault by GPU node-2

## Purpose

`MHCPreOp` and `MHCFusedPostPreOp` accept `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` and their callers expect a normalized `layer_input`. On `main` the unfused paths disagree about who applies that norm:

| path | applies the norm? |
|---|---|
| `forward_cuda` | yes, inside the fused kernel |
| `forward_hip` with AITER or TileLang | yes, inside the fused kernel |
| `forward_hip` fallback | yes, `_apply_mhc_norm` on top of `forward_native`'s output |
| `forward_native` | **no** — takes both parameters and ignores them |

`CustomOp.forward_oot` falls back to `forward_native`, so every out-of-tree backend loses the normalization. The failure is silent: nothing raises, no NaN appears, the numbers are just wrong.

I hit this running GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2. items.title: [Perf][Pooling] Avoid blocking seq_lens GPU-to-CPU copy for pooling in FlashInfer metadata builder
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
FlashInfer's metadata builder needs per-request sequence lengths on the CPU to plan paged KV metadata. For V2 model runner, `seq_lens` live on the GPU, so the builder fetches them with `common_attn_metadata.seq_lens.cpu()`. For pooling models this copy is avoidable; pooling models have no speculative tokens, so `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` maintained by the model runner is exact, not optimistic. The pooling runner already relies on this (`pooling_runner.py`: ["Pooling has no speculative tokens, so this CPU upper bound is exact"](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pool/pooling_runner.py#L142)). 

This results in a measured performance boost of about 1.35%.

AI assistance (locally hosted GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 as well as GPT-6 Astra) was used for implementation and analysis. All changed lines were reviewed and validated end-to-end.

## Test Plan

E2E benchmarking:

items.title: [ROCm] Enable Hisparse on ROCm : Sparse MLA Hot-Buffering
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).
HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

## Changes

**Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse
points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row
indices scale with total block count: max row index is 33 off HiSparse and 7.5M
on. AITER's decode kernel computes `row_index * row_width` in int32, so on
GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above row 3,728,270 and returns approximately
zero — no NaN, no assert. The Triton ragged path promotes the slot to
`tl.int64`, so under HiSparse it becomes unconditional, with
`allow_aiter_opus=False` so the prefill dispatcher cannot fall back into the
OPUS ASM kernel (same unverified addressing width). No flag, no env var.

**ROCm backend wiring.** CUDA HiSparse backends consume a dense `[tokens, topk]`
tensor; AITER's decode kernel consumes a ragged list plus indptr. Bridging that
is most of the diff: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` registers with an
`index_group_builder` (which is what makes `mla_attention.py` pick up
`hisparse_cache`), decode converts dense physical top-k to ragged and attends
against the hot buffer, and prefill stages host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
when the context is not fully resident. One new Triton kernel,
`compact_topk_to_ragged_triton` — `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable
because a mid-row `-1` must drop out rather than displace a valid entry.
AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse (its
buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
time); noted as a perf follow-up.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55351. The gfx950 low-M FP32 router GEMM added in #54845 never runs: `GateLinear` call sites (deepseek_v2, glm5next, deepseek_v4 nvidia/amd/cpu/xpu) pass the router dtype as `out_dtype` only, so the gate weight stays in the model dtype (bf16) and `allow_fp32_router_gemm` — which requires `self.weight.dtype == torch.float32` — is never true. The kernel is unreachable for the exact shapes it was instantiated for, e.g. DeepSeek-family `(6144, 256)`.

## Approach

Rather than updating every call site to pass `force_fp32_compute` (only nemotron_h does today), self-enable inside `GateLinear`: when `is_gfx950 and (input_size, output_size) in ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES and not bias`, set `force_fp32_compute = True` so the existing logic stores fp32 weights. One-site fix; the eligibility flags then light up through the normal path.

## What does NOT change

- CUDA paths (Hopper/Blackwell specialized kernels, bf16×bf16→fp32 epilogue): `is_gfx950` is false, guard inert.
- Unsupported shapes on gfx950 (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash's `(4096, 288)`): `is_rocm_fp32_shape` false, clean fallback.
- Biased gates: guard excludes bias (kernel/torch.mm path has no bias term).

## Verification

No GPU locally, so verified by simulation of the exact decision tree in `GateLinear.__init__`:

| Case | weights | fp32 kernel |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950, (6144, 256), no bias (issue repro) | fp32 | **enabled** (was: unreachable) |
| gfx950, (4096, 288) (GLM-5.3-Flash) | bf16 | unchanged fallback |
| CUDA H100, (6144, 256) | bf16 | unchanged |

items.title: [Bugfix] Invalidate KDA merged conv-weight cache on weight reload
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087. GLM-5.3 KDA merges the q/k/v short-conv weights into one cached tensor (`_merged_conv_weight`), built lazily on first forward. Online-RL workflows warm up with dummy weights (cache built), then refit `q_conv1d`/`k_conv1d`/`v_conv1d` — but the cached merge is never invalidated, so inference silently keeps using the pre-refit convolution weights.

## Approach

Weight loading dispatches on the param's stamped `weight_loader` (`getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` in `AutoWeightsLoader`). So the cache can be invalidated at exactly the point the weights change: in `Glm5NextLinearAttention.__init__`, wrap each conv weight's stamped loader so any write clears `_merged_conv_weight`. The next forward rebuilds it from the current params. No new hooks, no changes to the reload machinery.

## Coverage / limitations

- ✅ Initial load (loaders run before first forward; cache built after anyway)
- ✅ Checkpoint-format refit: `reload_weights` → `model.load_weights` → stamped loaders → cache cleared
- ✅ Layerwise reload: re-dispatches through the same stamped loaders
- ❌ Kernel-format refit (`param.copy_` bypass) writes params without loaders — the cache is NOT invalidated there. That path also skips every other derived-weight rebuild in the tree (same class of limitation); noted for follow-up if it matters in practice.

A `_version`-based approach was considered and rejected: the default loader writes via `param.data.copy_`, which bumps neither `param._version` nor `param.data._version` (verified on torch 2.10/ROCm), so version tracking cannot see the main refit path.

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

Pre-commit: all hooks pass. Single-node (TP-only) behavior is untouched — the guards only trigger when the target param is missing.

items.title: [Bugfix] Stop allocator fragmentation from shrinking the KV cache during memory profiling
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Wrap the memory-profiling forward pass in `Worker._scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20)`, the same scoped allocator setting #41268 applies around weight loading.

During `profile_run`, workspaces such as the MoE workspace grow in steps, and each step frees the previous, smaller buffer. With PyTorch's default (unlimited) `max_split_size_mb`, a later small allocation can be carved out of one of those freed multi-GiB blocks. That live block keeps the whole segment reserved through the `empty_cache()` in `memory_profiling`. The profiler measures consumption from free device memory, so the stranded segment is counted as consumed and taken out of the KV cache.

How much gets stranded depends on allocation order, so it varies per rank. With context parallelism the worst rank in each group sets the group's KV size, so the loss compounds. With a split limit, blocks above the limit are never split, so they stay whole and `empty_cache()` releases them. The limit is restored when the profiling pass exits, before `memory_profiling` measures, so serving and KV cache allocation run with the original allocator settings.

items.title: [Core] Add --release-weight-page-cache to drop checkpoint pages after load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

A DEP32 GLM-5.3 prefill group (4 pods x 8 DP ranks, DeepEP) dies as a unit: one rank stops between steps, the other 31 wait for it in `internode_dispatch`, hit the 100 s DeepEP timeout and trap (Xid 43); the stalled rank never traps. Captured on a production group right after its first real requests:

- The stalled worker's main thread was in kernel state `D` inside `__vm_munmap` for 73 s, ran for 1 s, then in a 16 KiB anonymous `mmap` (`vm_mmap_pgoff`) for 88 s. `py-spy` could not attach for exactly that window, since it needs `mmap_lock` as well.
- `perf` on the same workers under load: 1,000-3,400 `mmap` + `munmap` calls per second per worker, all 16 KiB. CPython 3.12 allocates a new frame data-stack chunk with `mmap` when a call crosses the end of the current chunk and frees it on return (python/cpython#142183, fixed in 3.13.13); the MoE forward crosses that boundary in every layer.
- The node sat at its free-memory floor for the whole stall: MemFree 16 GiB against MemAvailable 896 GiB (about 700 GiB of clean checkpoint pages plus a 761 GiB CPU KV tier in shm), with direct-reclaim bursts (`pgscan_direct` 7k-20k per 5 s), `compact_stall` 23-56 per 5 s and hundreds of `thp_fault_fallback`. `mmap` and `munmap` take the process `mmap_lock` for write; a page fault takes it for read and, with no free pages, holds it through direct reclaim and compaction. items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix index_kpool handling in FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## 1. Root cause

The FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA builder incorrectly used the main MLA cache's
`tokens_per_state` as the sparse indexer's `index_kpool`. These values describe
different layouts: GLM-5.3-Flash stores one main MLA cache state per token
(`tokens_per_state=1`), while its sparse indexer pools every four tokens
(`index_kpool=4`).

For example, with `index_topk=2048` and a context length of 2051, the indexer
produces 2048 selected token slots plus three tokens from the incomplete trailing
pool. The correct valid length is:

```text
2048 + 2051 % 4 = 2051
```

The old code instead calculated:

```text
2048 + 2051 % 1 = 2048
```

The three trailing slots were generated correctly but excluded from the length
passed to FlashInfer, so the kernel did not attend to them. Once the context
exceeds 2048, this can omit one to three recent tokens on three out of every four
decoding steps.

GSM8K did not expose the issue because every evaluated request stayed below 2048
tokens. In GPQA, it repeatedly trigges the incorrect length calculation.

## 2. Fix

Read `index_kpool` from the model configuration. Models without an `index_kpool`
value fall back to `1`, representing no pooling:

```python
index_kpool = getattr(hf_config, "index_kpool", None)
self._index_kpool = 1 if index_kpool is None else int(index_kpool)
```

## 3. Test results

All evaluations used GLM-5.3-Flash native FP8 weights, BF16 KV cache, TP8, no
speculative decoding, on H200.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.

## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

items.title: [Perf][Frontend] Linearize GLM tool-result rendering
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Remove quadratic tool-result validation and association from the default GLM chat-template rendering path.

The GLM-5.3 template repeatedly scans tool results and declared calls to check IDs and emit results in call order. Large **valid** tool-result blocks therefore take seconds to render, even when the results already arrive in the correct order. The [Hugging Face early-break update](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3/commit/aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42) helps some invalid blocks, but valid blocks still execute the nested scans.

This change:

- Validates and orders each tool-result block in Python using dictionaries and sets: expected O(C + R), for C calls and R result entries.
- Replaces only the template's tool-result ordering region with a linear rendering loop, preserving the remaining template and its formatting.
- Preserves call-order output for valid/partial blocks and received-order fallback for missing, duplicate, or unknown IDs, including nested result outputs.
- Returns a matched conversation/template pair without mutating caller-owned input. Only immutable rewritten templates are cached; requests and rendered outputs are not.
- Integrates in `safe_apply_chat_template`, shared by direct and executor-backed rendering. Explicit template overrides, continuation requests, unsupported architectures, and missing/ambiguous template anchors retain their original path.

The optimization is scoped to `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`. It adds no launch flags or dependencies, and uses no model-revision/hash allowlist. Full model templates and benchmark assets are not added to the repository.

**Related work:** adapted from [SGLang #36957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36957), with paired preparation/template selection, preserved fallback/nested-output behavior, and focused vLLM renderer regressions. An open-PR search on 2026-09-25 found no direct GLM ordering equivalent: [#39630]

This is the ROCm counterpart of #58684, which has the background.

On every build of `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with persistent metadata (the default for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x sparse MLA), `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` runs, decode steps included. ## Summary

Fixes #58727.

`AnthropicServingMessages.__init__` called `_detect_merge_inline_system(chat_template)` where `chat_template` is the CLI `--chat-template` override. For nearly every deployment that flag is not passed, so `chat_template` is `None` and `_detect_merge_inline_system` short-circuits to `True` without ever probing the actual template the renderer will use (the tokenizers `chat_template`). As a result, inline `role: "system"` messages were always hoisted into the leading system block, even for models (e.g. GLM-5.3) whose templates accept system messages in place. items.title: [Core] Bound draft-token RPC waits by the execute-model timeout
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`MultiprocExecutor.execute_model` and `sample_tokens` pass `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 300 s) to `collective_rpc`, but `take_draft_token_ids` does not. With spec decoding + structured outputs, the output-rank worker reads draft tokens back via `DraftTokensHandler.get_draft_tokens()` (`copy_event.synchronize()`). If that worker never replies, EngineCore blocks forever: no error, no worker cleanup, no recovery. This applies the same deadline so the stall reaches EngineCore's existing fatal-error and worker-shutdown path.

Not a duplicate: open PRs [#58279](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58279) (stale replies after worker errors) and [#54638](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54638) (worker-side watchdog) touch nearby failure handling, but neither bounds this RPC. This change is complementary.

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] persistent topk kernel loses candidates on overflow
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The persistent-topk kernel is race-y: it can lose winners in the case of overflow. This is not common (impossible at short enough context length), but when it does happen, it may (depending on the race winners) select worse completions than other runs that are identical in any other way. 

On a GB10, rows of 6000 to 32768 candidates with tight score distributions drop 89 to 6603 winners across five rows.

We can add detection for overflow which add one extra comparison/load on the hot paths for cases that do not overflow. On overflow, we select the bin's top members exactly with a byte-wise radix pass over the row. In the vast majority of cases this is not hit. No measurable cost was seen when running on ~200 runs (within +/- a few us).

`FilteredTopKUnifiedKernel` and `histogram_4096_topk` have the same buffer pattern on sm_90 and sm_100 and are not changed here. PRs to follow there.

Test included.

2. Existing top-k tests in that file, unchanged.
